question: Why is checking the baby's body temperature a high priority during early home visits?

options.A: High temperature proves the baby is exclusively breastfed
options.B: It is the only way to predict the adult height of the child
options.C: Newborns struggle to regulate heat and can easily develop hypothermia or fever
options.D: Normal room temperature makes infant checks unnecessary

explanation: Babies lose heat rapidly and lack mature temperature control, making thermal stability a key marker of health. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h4)

question: A newborn baby shows a strong palmar grasp on the right hand but has no response at all on the left hand after a difficult shoulder dystocia delivery. What condition does this finding most likely suggest?

options.A: General brain infection affecting both sides
options.B: Complete absence of the spinal cord
options.C: Normal variation in bilateral reflex strength
options.D: Brachial plexus injury on the left side

explanation: An asymmetric reflex following a difficult birth often points to nerve damage like a brachial plexus palsy on the weak side. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T6#BMP214_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which physical sign strongly suggests that the obstructed bowel has perforated?

options.A: A sudden return of loud, active bowel sounds
options.B: Passing a large amount of soft brown stool
options.C: A temporary spike in the patient's hunger level
options.D: A rigid, board-like abdomen with severe tenderness

explanation: When the bowel bursts and spills contents into the abdomen, the muscle wall tightens into severe rigidity (peritonitis). [learn more](BMP125_U3_T9#BMP125_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why is teaching manual milk expression important when a newborn has a weak sucking reflex?

options.A: To check if the mother has any breast infections
options.B: To maintain milk supply until the baby can feed directly
options.C: To prevent postpartum depression
options.D: To provide extra colostrum for the baby's skin

explanation: Regular milk removal stimulates hormones and keeps milk production going until the baby is strong enough to breastfeed. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T4#BMP214_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the best action if a child vomits while the mother is trying to give ORS with a spoon?

options.A: Mix extra salt into the next batch to stop the stomach upset.
options.B: Force a large cup of plain water to wash out the bitter taste.
options.C: Stop all fluid therapy completely and rush the child to the emergency ward.
options.D: Wait about ten minutes and then continue giving small sips more slowly.

explanation: Vomiting often subsides if fluids are given in tiny, patient amounts rather than large, rushed volumes. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T3#BMP222_U3_T3_h5)

question: How should a midwife care for the emotional needs of a woman experiencing a missed abortion?

options.A: Blame lifestyle choices to prevent future pregnancy losses
options.B: Focus strictly on physical procedures and avoid discussing feelings
options.C: Provide compassionate counseling and validate her feelings of grief
options.D: Advise her to forget the loss quickly because it was very early

explanation: A miscarriage is a real loss. Listening with empathy and validating the parents' grief helps support their emotional healing. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h7)

question: What blood pressure reading meets the basic diagnostic threshold for hypertension in preeclampsia?

options.A: 120/80 mmHg or higher
options.B: 160/110 mmHg or higher
options.C: 140/90 mmHg or higher
options.D: 130/85 mmHg or higher

explanation: Hypertension after 20 weeks is officially diagnosed when blood pressure reaches or exceeds 140/90 mmHg on two separate readings. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T4#BMP221_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common physical sign of an acute phobic panic reaction?

options.A: Rapid heart rate and pounding palpitations
options.B: Uncontrolled weight gain over several months
options.C: Shortness of breath and choking sensations
options.D: Trembling hands and sudden lightheadedness

explanation: Phobic reactions trigger sudden nervous system surges like rapid breathing and racing hearts, whereas gradual weight gain is a metabolic process. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T6#BMP223_U3_T6_h4)

question: What happens in the placental bed during the development of gestational hypertension?

options.A: Complete absence of maternal blood vessels
options.B: Rapid overgrowth of normal placental tissue
options.C: Inadequate invasion of maternal spiral arteries
options.D: Excessive widening of maternal spiral arteries

explanation: Poor trophoblast invasion means the spiral arteries remain narrow and high-resistance, restricting optimal blood flow to the placenta. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T2#BMP221_U3_T2_h2)

question: A midwife spelled a patient's surname wrong twenty times in a report. Which feature fixes this the fastest?

options.A: Undo and Redo
options.B: Format Painter
options.C: Find and Replace
options.D: Cut and Paste

explanation: Find and Replace scans the entire document for the incorrect spelling and updates every instance automatically in seconds. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the single most common cause of anemia in pregnant women globally?

options.A: Autoimmune hemolysis
options.B: Vitamin C shortage
options.C: Aplastic crisis
options.D: Iron deficiency

explanation: The body's iron stores are quickly depleted to meet the high metabolic demands of pregnancy and the growing baby. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T1#BMP221_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which qualitative method uses a facilitator to guide a group conversation about shared community views?

options.A: Randomized controlled trials
options.B: Structured laboratory surveys
options.C: Laboratory blood testing
options.D: Focus group discussions

explanation: Focus groups bring a small group of people together to talk about a topic so the researcher can observe group opinions and shared beliefs. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T3#BMP225_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is a core responsibility of a midwife in mental health promotion?

options.A: Forcing families to follow strict psychological treatment plans
options.B: Performing major psychiatric surgeries on postnatal patients
options.C: Educating mothers and families about normal emotional changes
options.D: Isolating depressed mothers from their newborn infants

explanation: Midwives help demystify the postpartum period by teaching mothers and their support systems what emotional changes to expect. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why do symptoms of uterine prolapse generally improve after the patient rests in bed?

options.A: Fluid retention in the lower body stops completely
options.B: Intra-abdominal pressure increases while sleeping
options.C: The pelvic muscles permanently repair themselves overnight
options.D: Gravity no longer pulls the pelvic organs downward

explanation: Horizontal positioning removes the downward gravitational pull on the unsupported uterus, temporarily relieving pressure. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h3)

question: How does tissue ischemia lead to fistula formation during difficult childbirth?

options.A: Compressed blood vessels starve the tissues of oxygen until they die and slough off
options.B: Rapid hormonal shifts cause the vaginal wall to dissolve during hard labor
options.C: Strong uterine contractions physically tear the front wall of the rectum open
options.D: Infected amniotic fluid eats directly through the muscle layers within minutes

explanation: Prolonged pressure compresses local blood vessels, causing ischemia and necrosis that eventually creates a hole between the two organs. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for advising a mother with mastitis to continue breastfeeding?

options.A: It prevents the baby from developing infant colic
options.B: It stops the mother's milk supply from drying up permanently
options.C: It helps drain the affected ducts and resolves the condition
options.D: It ensures the baby's daily vitamin intake is maintained

explanation: Removing milk frequently is the most effective way to clear the blockage and heal the inflamed tissue. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T6#BMP214_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of an acute Addisonian crisis?

options.A: Severe abdominal pain
options.B: High blood pressure
options.C: Extreme weakness
options.D: Profound hypotension

explanation: An Addisonian crisis causes dangerously low blood pressure (hypotension) and shock, not high blood pressure. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T7#BMP216_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why does punitive supervision often cause problems when working with community health workers?

options.A: It forces workers to undergo compulsory university education
options.B: It costs too much money for local government councils to maintain
options.C: It requires advanced computer systems to track minor errors
options.D: It drives workers away and discourages transparent reporting of complications

explanation: When supervisors are feared or overly harsh, community workers may hide mistakes or stop cooperating with the formal health system altogether. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T1#BMP316_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is surgery the appropriate management for a patient diagnosed with Asherman's syndrome?

options.A: Because the ovaries have stopped producing all circulating hormones
options.B: Because the condition involves physical scar tissue blocking the uterine cavity
options.C: Because the pituitary gland has developed a benign tumor
options.D: Because hormonal pills cannot be absorbed by women with this condition

explanation: Asherman's syndrome consists of intrauterine adhesions that require physical removal to restore the normal shape and function of the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why must you listen to bowel sounds before pressing on the abdomen during an exam?

options.A: Auscultation is the quickest part of the physical check
options.B: Palpation is painful and causes patients to stop the exam
options.C: Listening to the abdomen first warms up the stethoscope
options.D: Palpation can alter natural bowel sounds and peristalsis

explanation: Touching or pressing the abdomen can stimulate bowel motility, creating artificial sounds that do not reflect true baseline activity. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T1#BMP125_U3_T1_h2)

question: A patient treated twice for severe Pelvic Inflammatory Disease worries about future family planning. What is the midwife's best understanding of her situation?

options.A: Her ovaries will stop releasing eggs permanently because of chronic pelvic pain
options.B: Her risk of tubal factor infertility is significantly higher due to cumulative scar tissue
options.C: Her fertility will remain completely unaffected once the acute infection is cleared
options.D: Her uterus will no longer be able to produce enough progesterone for pregnancy

explanation: Each episode of PID causes more internal damage and scarring, drastically raising the long-term chance of blocked fallopian tubes and infertility. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T9#BMP310_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which specific medication is used for Intermittent Preventive Treatment for Malaria (IPTp) during pregnancy in Nigeria?

options.A: Quinine intravenous infusion
options.B: Chloroquine phosphate
options.C: Artemether-Lumefantrine
options.D: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine

explanation: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine, commonly abbreviated as SP, is the designated drug for IPTp in routine antenatal care guidelines. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is it necessary to leave the IUCD threads protruding two to three centimeters from the external os?

options.A: To signal when the copper wire has completely dissolved in the body
options.B: To serve as a wick for draining normal menstrual blood out of the uterus
options.C: To allow routine checking by the client and easy removal by the provider later
options.D: To anchor the device securely to the outer walls of the vagina

explanation: Leaving visible strings allows the client to check that the device is in place and gives the midwife something to pull during removal. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T4#BMP126_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why do pregnant and postpartum women often experience increased sweating?

options.A: Elevated metabolic rates and hormonal shifts
options.B: Decreased overall blood volume in the body
options.C: Sudden shrinkage of eccrine sweat ducts
options.D: Loss of sympathetic nervous system tone

explanation: Higher hormone levels and an increased metabolic workload during and after pregnancy naturally stimulate sweat gland activity. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T11#BMP111_U4_T11_h6)

question: Which regulatory body oversees professional nursing and midwifery practice in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Economics Association
options.B: National Union of Road Transport Workers
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Federal Ministry of Internal Affairs

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria sets the standards for training, practice, and professional conduct across the country. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h6)

question: What condition must be confirmed before an evisceration can be considered?

options.A: The baby is severely premature
options.B: The fetus is experiencing low oxygen
options.C: The fetus is confirmed dead
options.D: The baby has congenital anomalies

explanation: Destructive operations are only performed when the baby has already demised, as the procedure is not survivable for a living infant. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T7#BMP311_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which water source generally provides the best natural protection against surface contamination?

options.A: Shallow hand-dug well without a concrete apron
options.B: Open pond used collectively for cattle grazing
options.C: Fast-flowing river running through a village
options.D: Deep borehole tapping underground aquifers

explanation: Boreholes draw water from deep underground layers naturally filtered through thick soil and rock strata. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary physiological purpose of the endometrial cycle?

options.A: To stimulate mature egg release from the ovaries
options.B: To prepare the uterus for potential embryo implantation
options.C: To regulate daily basal body temperature changes
options.D: To maintain normal pelvic floor muscle tone

explanation: The monthly changes in the endometrial lining are specifically designed to create a fertile, receptive environment where a fertilized egg can successfully implant and grow. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T5#BMP210_U2_T5_h1)

question: What specific type of bone is the kneecap (patella) classified as?

options.A: Flat bone
options.B: Long bone
options.C: Irregular bone
options.D: Sesamoid bone

explanation: The patella develops inside a tendon, making it a classic sesamoid bone that improves mechanical leverage. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T13#BMP111_U2_T13_h4)

question: What are the classic signs of superficial thrombophlebitis in a varicose vein?

options.A: Sudden high fever accompanied by generalized body rashes
options.B: Localized pain, redness, and a tender hard cord along the vein
options.C: Complete numbness and coldness in the affected foot
options.D: Painless, clear fluid leaking directly through the skin

explanation: Thrombophlebitis involves inflammation and clotting in a surface vein, causing localized tenderness, redness, and a firm cord feeling. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T14#BMP212_U1_T14_h7)

question: A village elder is hesitant to let pregnant women visit the clinic due to custom. What is best to do first?

options.A: Report him to the police for obstructing essential public health services
options.B: Threaten to cut off all government food supplies to his household
options.C: Ignore his authority completely and open the clinic doors anyway
options.D: Approach him respectfully to discuss the health risks and build a shared solution

explanation: Respectful dialogue builds trust and helps leaders see the project as a shared benefit rather than a challenge to their authority. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is the Rubella vaccine never given to women who are currently pregnant?

options.A: It triggers immediate premature rupture of the membranes
options.B: It is completely ineffective during pregnancy
options.C: It causes severe allergic reactions in all pregnant women
options.D: It is a live vaccine that could potentially harm the developing baby

explanation: Rubella is a live-attenuated vaccine, so it is withheld during pregnancy and given safely after delivery if the mother lacks immunity. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h7)

question: What specialized solution is preferred over standard oral rehydration salt solution when treating dehydration in severe marasmus?

options.A: Plain sterile water with high sodium
options.B: Undiluted cow's milk with sugar
options.C: ReSoMal (Rehydration for Malnutrition)
options.D: Fruit juice with iron

explanation: ReSoMal has lower sodium and higher potassium than standard oral rehydration salt, which protects a weak heart from fluid overload. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which simple habit helps protect individuals from catching hookworm infections?

options.A: Wearing protective footwear outdoors
options.B: Avoiding all contact with sunlight
options.C: Sleeping under insecticide nets
options.D: Boiling all drinking water twice

explanation: Since hookworm larvae live in damp soil and penetrate bare skin, wearing shoes acts as an important barrier. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T10#BMP124_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why is placing a seizing or unstable pregnant patient in the left lateral position a standard emergency action?

options.A: It relieves pressure on the major blood vessels and prevents aspiration
options.B: It is the only comfortable sleeping position allowed in the hospital
options.C: It stops uterine contractions permanently without needing drugs
options.D: It allows the doctor to perform an immediate vaginal examination

explanation: The left lateral position stops the uterus from pressing on the inferior vena cava, keeping blood flowing to the heart and stopping vomit from entering the lungs. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h6)

question: What major health problem is directly linked to open defecation?

options.A: Contamination of soil and water sources leading to severe infections
options.B: Rapid depletion of underground mineral deposits in the local community
options.C: Sudden outbreaks of airborne respiratory infections like tuberculosis
options.D: Severe vitamin deficiency disorders among growing infants and children

explanation: Open defecation leaves human waste exposed where rain washes it directly into water sources and soil, spreading dangerous gastrointestinal diseases. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h3)

question: A 55-year-old market trader presents with symptoms of uterine prolapse after years of carrying heavy loads on her head. Why does heavy lifting contribute to this condition?

options.A: It prevents normal blood circulation to the pelvic bones
options.B: It chronically increases intra-abdominal pressure downward
options.C: It rapidly depletes systemic estrogen levels in women
options.D: It causes direct trauma to the cervix during movement

explanation: Straining and lifting force intra-abdominal contents downward against a pelvic floor that may already be weakened. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h2)

question: When is it necessary to use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Every time you enter a postnatal ward
options.B: Immediately after taking a patient's temperature
options.C: When hands are visibly soiled with blood or body fluids
options.D: Before performing an aseptic wound dressing

explanation: Visible dirt or fluid stops alcohol from reaching and killing microorganisms effectively. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h3)

question: A clinic runs out of condoms and youth contraceptives. What practical step should the midwife take first?

options.A: Tell young clients to purchase adult supplies abroad
options.B: Stop offering reproductive health counseling entirely
options.C: Refer all young clients to traditional birth attendants
options.D: Advocate for resupply through local health supply chains

explanation: Midwives must proactively manage supplies and request resupplies to keep services running smoothly. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T5#BMP320_U3_T5_h7)

question: How many of Amsel's signs must be present to diagnose bacterial vaginosis clinically?

options.A: At least two
options.B: At least three
options.C: Only one
options.D: All four

explanation: A reliable clinical diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis requires at least three out of the four Amsel criteria. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why is breast milk alone not enough for a baby after six months of age?

options.A: The infant's nutritional demands for iron and zinc exceed what breast milk provides
options.B: Maternal antibodies disappear entirely from the mother's body
options.C: Breast milk completely dries up and stops production after six months
options.D: Infants completely lose their ability to digest human milk proteins

explanation: Rapid growth after six months increases mineral needs, especially iron and zinc, beyond what breast milk alone provides. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T3#BMP118_U3_T3_h1)

question: How do recurrent infections like frequent malaria and diarrhea negatively affect a child's growth?

options.A: They stop the absorption of water while keeping all food intact
options.B: They reduce appetite and drain nutrients, leading to weight loss
options.C: They permanently increase the child's daily metabolic calorie needs
options.D: They cause the child's bones to fuse prematurely at an early age

explanation: Infections suppress appetite and increase metabolic demands, causing nutritional deficits. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T2#BMP222_U1_T2_h8)

question: A student wants a free, customizable operating system to learn programming. Which system fits best?

options.A: Windows
options.B: Linux
options.C: macOS
options.D: Proprietary console OS

explanation: Linux is free, open-source, highly customizable, and serves as the standard platform for learning programming and server administration. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T1#BMP123_U2_T1_h6)

question: What does the maternal mortality ratio specifically measure?

options.A: Total number of women who experience a miscarriage in a community clinic
options.B: Percentage of babies born with a low birth weight in a local health zone
options.C: Deaths of women during pregnancy or shortly after per 100,000 live births
options.D: Number of pregnant women who fail to register for antenatal care services

explanation: The maternal mortality ratio calculates deaths related to pregnancy or childbirth per 100,000 live births to show maternal health risk. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T4#BMP227_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why should facility staff hold internal review meetings before sending their monthly reports?

options.A: To train new security guards on basic record keeping.
options.B: To spot discrepancies and resolve inconsistencies together.
options.C: To celebrate the end of another stressful working month.
options.D: To dispose of old paper registers by burning them safely.

explanation: Team reviews allow colleagues to cross-check numbers and fix mistakes before the report leaves the clinic doors. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h4)

question: Placing a newborn directly onto a cold metal weighing scale without a protective cloth causes heat loss through which method?

options.A: Convection
options.B: Radiation
options.C: Conduction
options.D: Evaporation

explanation: Conduction occurs when body heat is transferred directly to a colder solid object touching the baby's skin. [learn more](BMP214_U2_T1#BMP214_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why are height and weight measurements routinely taken during school physical screenings?

options.A: To plot growth charts and identify malnutrition like stunting or wasting
options.B: To measure how fast a child's brain is developing academically
options.C: To determine which children are qualified to join school sports teams only
options.D: To calculate the exact daily school fee each parent should pay

explanation: Anthropometric measurements track physical growth over time, helping nurses spot signs of chronic malnutrition or nutritional excess early. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h4)

question: How long do the mild emotional symptoms of the baby blues typically last before resolving on their own?

options.A: Throughout the entire pregnancy
options.B: Up to six months
options.C: About two weeks
options.D: Exactly one year

explanation: The baby blues are short-lived hormonal mood shifts that resolve quickly within the first fourteen days after delivery, unlike true clinical depression. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T2#BMP223_U2_T2_h1)

question: A laboring woman receiving oxytocin develops six contractions in 10 minutes accompanied by late decelerations in the fetal heart rate. What is the immediate action the midwife should take?

options.A: Prepare the patient for an immediate routine vaginal examination
options.B: Stop the oxytocin infusion immediately and reposition the patient
options.C: Administer a dose of oral pain medication and wait 15 minutes
options.D: Increase the oxytocin infusion rate to speed up delivery

explanation: Frequent contractions and late decelerations indicate uterine hyperstimulation and fetal distress; stopping the oxytocin removes the stimulus and lateral positioning improves oxygen flow. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T1#BMP213_U1_T1_h6)

question: A postpartum patient with severe pre-eclampsia has blood trickling continuously from old IV sites and low urine output. What should the midwife suspect first?

options.A: Acute tubular necrosis from dehydration
options.B: An allergic reaction to oxytocin infusion
options.C: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
options.D: Normal physiological postpartum diuresis

explanation: The combination of abnormal bleeding from puncture sites and declining urine output strongly points toward developing DIC. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T6#BMP311_U4_T6_h3)

question: A patient scheduled for a planned caesarean at 9:00 AM asks for tea at 7:00 AM. What should you do?

options.A: Allow clear tea without milk because it digests easily before surgery
options.B: Permit the tea if she promises to vomit before entering the theater
options.C: Refuse the request and explain the danger of aspiration during anesthesia
options.D: Call the doctor to prescribe a strong laxative instead of the tea

explanation: Patients must remain fasting before surgery to prevent stomach contents from entering the lungs if anesthesia causes vomiting. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T4#BMP311_U3_T4_h3)

question: Where are members of the Enterobacteriaceae family naturally found in the human body?

options.A: Bloodstream
options.B: Lungs
options.C: Intestines
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Enteric bacteria are normal inhabitants of the human gastrointestinal tract, living there safely until they spread to other tissues. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T6#BMP116_U2_T6_h2)

question: A non-immune mother receives the rubella vaccine immediately after delivery. What crucial advice should the midwife give her?

options.A: Avoid breastfeeding your newborn baby entirely
options.B: Keep the child away from sunlight
options.C: Take high doses of antibiotics starting today
options.D: Delay getting pregnant again for at least one month

explanation: Because the vaccine contains a live attenuated virus, women are advised to avoid pregnancy for a short window after receipt to protect a potential fetus. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T3#BMP222_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is BBT tracking alone limited when used by a couple trying to avoid pregnancy?

options.A: It increases the total number of days in the menstrual cycle
options.B: It stops working once a woman turns thirty years old
options.C: It only confirms ovulation after it has already occurred
options.D: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to read daily

explanation: Because BBT only shows that ovulation happened in the past, it does not give advance warning before the fertile window opens. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T4#BMP224_U4_T4_h5)

question: A patient with a history of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease presents with sharp, one-sided lower abdominal pain and spotting after a missed period. What condition should be suspected first?

options.A: Ectopic pregnancy
options.B: Normal intrauterine pregnancy
options.C: Primary ovarian failure
options.D: Acute appendicitis

explanation: Unilateral pain, missed menses, and a history of PID are classic red flags for a tubal ectopic pregnancy, which can rupture and cause severe internal bleeding. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T9#BMP310_U3_T9_h4)

question: What does an LSIL result typically mean on a lab report?

options.A: Large spreading invasive malignant tumor of the uterus
options.B: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion with mild dysplasia
options.C: Complete absence of any epithelial cells on the slide
options.D: Normal tissue with zero inflammation or cellular changes

explanation: LSIL stands for low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, which shows mild, often temporary cell changes from HPV. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why is it risky for a midwife to ignore informal community groups?

options.A: It automatically violates national health insurance laws and policies
options.B: It can lead to low community participation and rejection of health programs
options.C: It prevents the midwife from receiving her monthly government salary
options.D: It stops the construction of new maternity wards in the district

explanation: People look to their trusted local groups for guidance. Ignoring these groups means the community may disregard your health initiatives. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T1#BMP117_U2_T1_h3)

question: What should a midwife do first when a newly delivered mother wants to walk to the bathroom for the very first time?

options.A: Lock the bathroom door from the outside for safety
options.B: Accompany and physically support her during the walk
options.C: Leave the room so she can maintain her personal privacy
options.D: Tell her to run quickly so she finishes before getting tired

explanation: Being right there to support a weak mother prevents sudden dizziness from turning into a dangerous fall. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h2)

question: A newly delivered mother feels useless because she needs help bathing and changing her baby. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Guide her gently through tasks at her own pace and praise her efforts
options.B: Ask a relative to take over baby care duties until she goes home
options.C: Tell her that every new mother feels this way and leave the room
options.D: Take over completely so she does not feel stressed by failure

explanation: Involving the mother in small steps builds her confidence and restores her sense of competence and self-esteem. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T4#BMP110_U1_T4_h6)

question: What page setup feature ensures that column header labels repeat at the top of every printed page?

options.A: Portrait orientation
options.B: Print Title Rows
options.C: Formula auditing
options.D: Auto-fit cell width

explanation: Setting repeat title rows keeps your column headers visible across multi-page printouts for easier reading. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T2#BMP123_U3_T2_h7)

question: A primary health clinic notices low antenatal clinic attendance. What is the best community approach to address this?

options.A: Close the clinic down until community members start coming voluntarily
options.B: Report all pregnant women who miss appointments to local police officers
options.C: Hold a town hall meeting with local leaders and women to discuss barriers
options.D: Print posters in English and place them inside the locked clinic doors

explanation: Engaging the community directly through dialogue helps uncover the real reasons behind low attendance so collaborative solutions can be found. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T5#BMP117_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why can severe untreated neonatal jaundice lead to long-term developmental impairment?

options.A: It prevents the infant from absorbing breast milk nutrients in the gut
options.B: High levels of bilirubin can cross the blood-brain barrier and damage neural tissue
options.C: It permanently damages the skin cells responsible for vitamin D production
options.D: It causes the infant to stop breathing entirely within the first week of life

explanation: Excess unconjugated bilirubin is neurotoxic and can cause kernicterus, resulting in lifelong motor and cognitive deficits. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T4#BMP222_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is close monitoring needed when giving intravenous labetalol for severe pre-eclampsia?

options.A: To ensure the intravenous cannula never leaks fluid onto skin
options.B: To measure the exact volume of urine produced every minute
options.C: To prevent blood pressure from dropping too fast or too low
options.D: To check if the patient is developing gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Intravenous medication acts quickly, so tight monitoring is vital to avoid dropping the mother's blood pressure too drastically. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h5)

question: How many blood vessels should a midwife normally see when inspecting the cut surface of the umbilical cord?

options.A: Three arteries and two veins
options.B: One large artery and one vein
options.C: Two arteries and one vein
options.D: Two veins and one artery

explanation: A normal umbilical cord contains three vessels, consisting of a pair of arteries carrying deoxygenated blood and a single vein carrying oxygenated blood. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T3#BMP212_U3_T3_h3)

question: In what direction do water molecules move during osmosis?

options.A: From low water concentration to high water concentration
options.B: From high water concentration to low water concentration
options.C: From inside the blood vessels straight out to the bones
options.D: From areas of high pressure to areas of low temperature

explanation: Water naturally travels down its concentration gradient, flowing where it is most abundant to where it is less abundant. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T4#BMP111_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why must midwives view a high-risk pregnancy condition as dynamic rather than fixed?

options.A: Patients usually fake their symptoms to stay longer in the ward
options.B: Laboratory values change strictly according to the time of day
options.C: A stable condition can rapidly deteriorate into an emergency
options.D: Hospital policies require daily reassessment of room assignments

explanation: Conditions like gestational diabetes or pre-eclampsia can worsen suddenly, meaning constant vigilance is required from the midwifery team. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is checking the hemoglobin level important before treating a missed abortion?

options.A: It measures the exact hormonal output of the failing placenta
options.B: It proves whether the patient has an active bacterial infection
options.C: Baseline anemia is common, and treatment may involve blood loss
options.D: High hemoglobin levels completely prevent the need for any surgery

explanation: Many women already have low blood counts due to nutritional anemia, so it is vital to check hemoglobin before any procedure that might cause bleeding. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why are antiviral drugs sometimes given in the third trimester to pregnant women with Hepatitis B?

options.A: To stop the mother from experiencing morning sickness and fatigue
options.B: To prevent the baby from developing gestational diabetes in the womb
options.C: To lower the viral load and reduce the risk of passing the infection to the baby
options.D: To completely cure the mother of chronic Hepatitis B before delivery

explanation: Lowering the amount of virus in the mother's blood with medication helps protect the newborn during birth. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T7#BMP221_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of bedside teaching in midwifery?

options.A: To test students without supervision
options.B: To replace traditional classroom lectures entirely
options.C: To connect theoretical knowledge with practical patient care
options.D: To reduce the workload of senior staff nurses

explanation: Bedside teaching brings classroom concepts directly to the ward so students can see and practice real care. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why are combined estrogen-progestogen birth control methods generally avoided during the first three weeks after birth?

options.A: They increase the risk of blood clots and can reduce milk supply
options.B: They accelerate the natural involution of the uterine muscle
options.C: They cause immediate permanent cessation of lochia flow
options.D: They make the infant hypersensitive to synthetic hormones

explanation: Postpartum women already have a higher chance of developing blood clots, and estrogen adds to this risk while also slowing down milk production. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h5)

question: A mother says her two-day-old baby boy is refusing feeds and sleeping much more than usual. What should the midwife suspect?

options.A: Early-onset neonatal sepsis
options.B: Congenital heart defect alone
options.C: Neonatal tetanus due to cutting
options.D: Normal newborn adjustment

explanation: Poor feeding and unusual sleepiness in the first days of life are key warning signs of early-onset neonatal sepsis. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h4)

question: What does the principle of clinical equipoise mean in experimental midwifery research?

options.A: The researchers must be neutral observers who never speak to patients
options.B: All participants must pay equal amounts of money for their hospital care
options.C: The experimental group must always be larger than the control group
options.D: There must be genuine uncertainty about which treatment is better before starting

explanation: Equipoise means researchers must genuinely not know whether the new treatment or standard care is superior, making it fair to test both. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T4#BMP225_U2_T4_h5)

question: How should a midwife correctly handwrite a bacterial scientific name in a clinical logbook?

options.A: Capitalize both the genus and the species names equally
options.B: Underline the genus and species names separately
options.C: Italicize both words using a standard ballpoint pen
options.D: Write both words entirely in capital letters without marks

explanation: When handwriting scientific names where italics cannot be used, standard convention requires underlining the genus and species separately. [learn more](BMP116_U1_T2#BMP116_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which management function involves checking if work is being done according to set rules and goals?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Coordinating
options.C: Controlling
options.D: Commanding

explanation: Controlling is the process of monitoring ongoing activities to make sure performance matches established standards and goals. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T2#BMP312_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why are home visits important when a mother leaves the hospital very early after birth?

options.A: They force the family to purchase extra hospital equipment
options.B: They allow the midwife to permanently reside with the family
options.C: They guarantee that the baby will never catch any childhood illness
options.D: They bridge the gap to ensure continuity of care after leaving the facility

explanation: Early discharge can leave mothers vulnerable before complications fully show, making home visits essential for ongoing monitoring. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the best immediate response when a sudden rainstorm disrupts an open-air health education lecture?

options.A: Continue teaching loudly in the rain until the participants leave
options.B: Send all the participants home and postpone the campaign for a month
options.C: Blame the community leaders for failing to check the weather forecast
options.D: Flexibly relocate the session to a nearby covered venue or classroom

explanation: Field execution requires adaptability, such as quickly shifting venues to keep the audience engaged and dry. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T1#BMP227_U2_T1_h5)

question: When is a surgical option like a hysterectomy usually considered for metrorrhagia?

options.A: Whenever a woman wants to preserve her ability to have children
options.B: When medical treatments fail and the woman has completed her family
options.C: Only when laboratory tests confirm mild iron-deficiency
options.D: As the first treatment option for every teenage patient

explanation: Major surgeries such as a hysterectomy are kept for severe cases that do not respond to medications, particularly when the patient no longer wishes to have children. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T4#BMP310_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer from stage IIB to IVA?

options.A: Concurrent chemoradiation
options.B: Cryotherapy alone
options.C: Hormone replacement therapy
options.D: Simple abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: Advanced tumors that have spread beyond the cervix respond much better to a combination of radiation and chemotherapy than to surgery. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why does a midwife in Nigeria need to look beyond the clinic walls to understand maternal health?

options.A: Community members refuse to visit clinics unless forced by traditional rulers
options.B: Home environments and cultural practices heavily influence health-seeking habits
options.C: Midwives are legally required to live in the village where they work
options.D: Hospital records are always completely accurate without needing outside checks

explanation: Things outside the clinic, like transport and local traditions, strongly affect how and when women decide to seek maternity care. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three core rules required for LAM to remain effective?

options.A: The mother remains completely amenorrheic past eight weeks
options.B: Nursing happens frequently throughout both day and night
options.C: The baby feeds exclusively or near-exclusively on breast milk
options.D: The infant receives regular formula feeds daily

explanation: Formula feeding introduces intervals and substances that disrupt the suckling feedback loop, meaning regular formula feeding violates LAM rules. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T5#BMP224_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard comfort measure for an unconscious, dying patient?

options.A: Repositioning gently to prevent pressure ulcers
options.B: Ensuring a quiet and peaceful room environment
options.C: Keeping the lips and oral mucosa moist with water
options.D: Administering aggressive daily iron supplements

explanation: Iron supplements provide no comfort in terminal stages and do nothing to relieve end-of-life distress. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T2#BMP120_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which physical sign is a reliable indicator of moderate to severe fluid loss in infants?

options.A: Flushed and moist facial skin
options.B: Sunken eyes and absent tears
options.C: Rapid and bounding peripheral pulses
options.D: Bulging anterior fontanelle

explanation: Fluid volume deficits reduce fat turgor around the eyes and tear gland secretions, causing sunken eyes and dry crying. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T2#BMP222_U3_T2_h2)

question: What infant feeding practice is recommended for mothers on ART with a suppressed viral load in Nigeria?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months
options.B: Mixed feeding with breast milk and water from birth
options.C: Immediate formula feeding from day one after birth
options.D: Early introduction of solid family foods at two months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding combined with maternal ART provides the best health outcomes while minimizing the risk of HIV transmission. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T6#BMP213_U4_T6_h5)

question: How do Community Health Committees help improve local health facilities?

options.A: By closing down clinics that do not meet international standards
options.B: By taking over the daily clinical duties of the resident midwives
options.C: By mobilizing community support for maintenance and resolving staff-patient grievances
options.D: By preventing community members from visiting formal hospitals

explanation: CHCs act as administrators and peacebuilders, keeping clinics functional and fostering good relationships. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is a defining characteristic of a voluntary psychiatric admission?

options.A: The court orders the patient to stay in the hospital for observation
options.B: The patient requests treatment and retains the right to ask for discharge
options.C: The patient is locked in a secure ward without access to visitors
options.D: Family members make all medical decisions on behalf of the patient

explanation: Voluntary patients enter the hospital of their own accord and keep the right to request leaving, provided they are not a danger. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T4#BMP223_U1_T4_h2)

question: A clinic has a cockroach problem in the kitchen. Following IPM principles, what should be done first?

options.A: Introduce predatory fish into the kitchen sink drains
options.B: Ignore the pests until they disappear on their own
options.C: Identify food sources, clean thoroughly, and seal cracks
options.D: Evacuate the entire clinic and spray industrial poison

explanation: IPM prioritizes sanitation and environmental modifications before resorting to chemical insecticides. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T3#BMP117_U4_T3_h6)

question: How should a midwife respond when a client fears modern contraceptives cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Explain gently with facts about how fertility returns after stopping
options.B: Scold the client for listening to uneducated neighborhood gossips
options.C: Refuse to provide any services until the myth is completely forgotten
options.D: Prescribe stronger hormonal drugs to counteract the imagined damage

explanation: Patient education delivered with empathy helps clear up misunderstandings without making the client feel foolish or judged. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T4#BMP224_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why is accurate documentation in the official child health card important for clinical practice?

options.A: It prevents the family from ever moving to another state or clinic.
options.B: It ensures continuity of care when different health workers see the child.
options.C: It acts as a legal identity card for entering primary school classes.
options.D: It serves as a receipt for paying government health insurance levies.

explanation: Well-kept records allow any clinician reviewing the card later to understand the child's past growth history and health status immediately. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T3#BMP222_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which intervention should a midwife prioritize first for an overweight patient with early knee osteoarthritis?

options.A: Strict bed rest to prevent any further friction on the bones
options.B: Immediate scheduling for total knee replacement surgery
options.C: Guided weight reduction and low-impact exercise education
options.D: Intravenous administration of high-dose systemic steroids

explanation: Lifestyle changes like weight loss and strengthening exercises reduce joint stress and form the foundation of osteoarthritis management. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of marasmus in young infants?

options.A: Diluted and low-calorie cereal gruels
options.B: Early stopping of breast milk
options.C: Recurrent diarrhea infections
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding for six months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding protects against malnutrition. Stopping it early and giving poor foods triggers marasmus. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h2)

question: What does routine urinalysis primarily check for during an antenatal visit?

options.A: Electrolyte balance and liver enzymes
options.B: Red blood cell shape and size
options.C: Protein, glucose, and infection
options.D: Hormone levels and ovulation

explanation: Urine dipsticks quickly reveal protein for pre-eclampsia, glucose for diabetes, and white cells for infection. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h2)

question: How do midwives and community health nurses bridge the gap in child health?

options.A: By connecting families, schools, and primary health care clinics
options.B: By building private hospitals inside every school compound
options.C: By replacing classroom teachers during school hours permanently
options.D: By forbidding parents from visiting the school premises

explanation: The nurse serves as the bridge, ensuring health findings from school screenings reach parents and are followed up at local health facilities. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h6)

question: What common issue do teachers often notice during long, uninterrupted lectures?

options.A: Learners become overly aggressive and demand extra assignments
options.B: Student attention and concentration drop significantly over time
options.C: Attendance drops to zero within the first five minutes
options.D: Students instantly master all practical delivery room procedures

explanation: Human attention spans are limited, so listening passively for too long naturally leads to tiredness and zoning out. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why should oxytocin infusion be delayed until suction evacuation has started in molar pregnancies?

options.A: To stop the blood hCG levels from dropping too quickly
options.B: To allow the cervix enough time to close tightly around instruments
options.C: To ensure the patient experiences maximum pain relief during the procedure
options.D: To prevent forcing molar tissue into the maternal blood vessels

explanation: Contracting the uterus prematurely before evacuation begins can drive tumor emboli into the maternal circulation, leading to severe pulmonary complications. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h5)

question: A patient recovering from acute gastritis asks about the best eating pattern. What should the midwife advise?

options.A: Fast completely for several days after discharge
options.B: Eat small, frequent meals throughout the day
options.C: Consume only extremely spicy foods to clear the stomach
options.D: Eat one large heavy meal once daily in the evening

explanation: Small, frequent meals prevent the stomach from overstretching and reduce excessive acid secretion caused by large meals. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T4#BMP125_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which type of antifungal medication is typically required to treat severe, life-threatening fungal infections?

options.A: Low-dose clotrimazole cream
options.B: Over-the-counter sulfur dusting powder
options.C: Intravenous amphotericin B
options.D: Gentian violet topical paint

explanation: Deep systemic infections require potent intravenous medications like amphotericin B to reach internal organs and save the mother's life. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T8#BMP124_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard preventive measure for tetanus in children?

options.A: Immunizing pregnant women with tetanus toxoid
options.B: Proper cleansing and care of skin wounds
options.C: Giving daily routine antifungal tablets
options.D: Routine childhood immunization schedules

explanation: Antifungal medications have no role in preventing tetanus, which is a bacterial infection prevented through vaccines and wound hygiene. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T7#BMP222_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why do healthcare workers monitor adolescent males with mumps closely for testicular pain?

options.A: To measure the exact growth rate of facial hair
options.B: To check if the kidneys are producing enough urine
options.C: To prevent the permanent loss of their appendix
options.D: To detect orchitis, a painful inflammation of the testes

explanation: Orchitis is a well-known post-pubertal complication of mumps that causes sudden testicular swelling, severe pain, and tenderness. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T2#BMP222_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of holding a mock OSCE before the real exam?

options.A: To save money on clinical training equipment
options.B: To permanently replace final board certification exams
options.C: To remove the fear of the unknown through practice
options.D: To test how many students can fail in one afternoon

explanation: Mock exams familiarize students with the physical layout, timing, and pressure of the actual OSCE environment. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h7)

question: Why are regular audits helpful for a busy maternity ward?

options.A: They uncover inefficiencies, prevent theft, and ensure policy compliance
options.B: They automatically increase the annual government health budget
options.C: They replace the daily nursing handover process
options.D: They eliminate the need for midwives to document patient care

explanation: Audits provide a systematic check that discourages financial dishonesty and highlights where resources are leaking. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T3#BMP312_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which hormone is released by the hypothalamus to start the pubertal cascade?

options.A: Human Growth Hormone
options.B: Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone
options.C: Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone
options.D: Adrenocorticotropic Hormone

explanation: GnRH is the master hormone secreted by the hypothalamus that signals the pituitary gland to release LH and FSH, starting puberty. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the main goal of assessing a postpartum client for LAM during a routine clinic visit?

options.A: To register her infant for routine childhood immunizations and vitamin drops
options.B: To calculate the exact financial savings she achieves by not buying formula
options.C: To teach her how to produce more milk volume for a fast-growing infant
options.D: To confirm she meets all three strict criteria before relying on it for birth control

explanation: Midwives must carefully verify amenorrhea, exclusive feeding, and frequency to ensure the client is fully protected against unintended pregnancy. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T5#BMP224_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why must midwives apply universal precautions even if a woman looks healthy and has a negative antenatal test?

options.A: Healthy women carry higher bacterial loads than sick patients
options.B: Hospital policy requires it only for statistical record keeping
options.C: Antenatal tests can miss very recent infections or window periods
options.D: Ministry of health laws punish midwives who skip documentation

explanation: A negative test at 36 weeks does not protect against an infection contracted just before labor during the window period. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary fetal risk linked to high-dose oral fluconazole use in early pregnancy?

options.A: Severe permanent infant hearing loss
options.B: Complete closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.C: Immediate premature rupture of membranes
options.D: Craniofacial and skeletal birth defects

explanation: High and continuous doses of oral fluconazole in the first trimester are linked to rare bone and skull malformations in the baby. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T8#BMP124_U4_T8_h4)

question: What common side effect should a midwife warn a patient to expect during the first few days of taking methyldopa?

options.A: Insomnia
options.B: Hyperactivity
options.C: Excessive sweating
options.D: Drowsiness

explanation: Sedation and drowsiness are very common when first starting methyldopa or increasing the dose. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of using only the built-in spelling and grammar checker for medical documents?

options.A: It only functions when the computer is connected to a printer
options.B: It changes the font style of the entire document without warning
options.C: It permanently deletes words it does not recognize
options.D: It may flag correct specialized medical terms as errors

explanation: Standard dictionary software is built for general language and often fails to recognize uncommon clinical terms and drug names. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why does a red blood cell undergo crenation when placed in a hypertonic solution?

options.A: Water rushes inside the cell until the plasma membrane stretches apart
options.B: Water flows out of the cell into the surrounding hypertonic liquid
options.C: Solutes from the outside environment enter the cytoplasm to cause swelling
options.D: Cellular proteins actively pump out all remaining internal water molecules

explanation: Hypertonic surroundings draw water out of the red blood cell, causing it to shrink and wrinkle up. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T4#BMP111_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which organism forms a stubborn protective layer (biofilm) on vaginal walls during bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Gardnerella vaginalis
options.C: Treponema pallidum
options.D: Herpes simplex virus

explanation: Gardnerella vaginalis is a main organism in bacterial vaginosis that creates a dense biofilm, making the infection harder to treat. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h2)

question: Why are practical skills assessments so important in busy maternity units?

options.A: It removes the need for any future training
options.B: High patient numbers mean every student must master procedures to keep care safe
options.C: Patients refuse care without a laminated card
options.D: Government rules require daily written tests

explanation: Busy wards expose students to many cases, making proper skills checks essential for maintaining high standards and patient safety. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h1)

question: A pregnant woman attending antenatal clinic at 24 weeks gestation is prescribed sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine. What is the primary clinical goal?

options.A: Prevention of congenital syphilis transmission
options.B: Routine eradication of intestinal hookworms
options.C: Emergency treatment for acute cerebral malaria
options.D: Intermittent Preventive Treatment for malaria

explanation: IPTp-SP is administered at routine intervals during pregnancy to reduce the burden of malaria and its adverse outcomes. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T3#BMP116_U3_T3_h7)

question: What should a midwife do if an implant is inserted too deeply and cannot be felt?

options.A: Prescribe oral antibiotics and wait for it to push out
options.B: Leave the rod inside the arm forever without action
options.C: Refer the client to a specialist for imaging-guided removal
options.D: Make a large deep cut across the entire upper arm

explanation: Deeply placed implants require specialized surgical skills and imaging tools to locate and remove safely without nerve damage. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T7#BMP224_U3_T7_h6)

question: Why is leaving an active EHR terminal unlocked in a busy ward dangerous?

options.A: Unauthorized persons can view or tamper with patient files
options.B: The hospital internet service provider will block the IP address
options.C: Automatic software updates will fail to install properly
options.D: The computer battery will drain much faster than usual

explanation: An unattended, logged-in workstation breaks data security protocols, exposing confidential patient files to anyone walking past. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T2#BMP123_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why should midwives avoid applying tight improvised bandages to a newborn with clubfoot?

options.A: It prevents the mother from breastfeeding successfully
options.B: It permanently fuses the bones in the wrong position
options.C: It can damage fragile skin and restrict blood circulation
options.D: It speeds up bone growth too quickly in the joint

explanation: Newborn skin is very delicate, and tight wrapping risks causing pressure sores or cutting off blood supply. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h3)

question: What should a midwife do first after sustaining a deep needle-stick injury during episiotomy repair?

options.A: Swallow prophylactic antiretroviral drugs kept in the ward locker
options.B: Wash the wound with soap and running water after encouraging bleeding
options.C: Squeeze the puncture site tightly and apply a strong iodine tincture
options.D: Cover the bleeding finger with a plaster and finish the skin sutures

explanation: Washing under running water helps flush out pathogens introduced by the sharp object before starting official reporting and PEP protocols. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which scan gives the most accurate measurement of cervical length in the second trimester?

options.A: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic X-ray
options.C: Manual digital examination
options.D: Routine abdominal ultrasound

explanation: Placing the ultrasound probe close to the cervix via the vagina gives a clear and precise view of its length and internal shape. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h4)

question: How does falling estrogen contribute to hot flashes?

options.A: It damages the sweat glands in the skin
options.B: It narrows the thermoneutral zone of the brain
options.C: It increases the total amount of body fat stores
options.D: It stops the heart from pumping blood to the skin

explanation: A narrowed thermoneutral zone makes the body overreact to tiny temperature changes, triggering sudden heat release. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T2#BMP320_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must community midwives build strong relationships with traditional birth attendants?

options.A: To arrest them for illegal medical practices
options.B: To take over their traditional revenue streams
options.C: To force them out of rural settlements completely
options.D: To encourage early referral and teamwork for safe births

explanation: Working alongside local birth attendants helps build trust and ensures women experiencing complications are sent to the midwife early. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T2#BMP316_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the minimum hourly urine output needed to show the kidneys are getting enough blood during shock management?

options.A: 60 millilitres per hour
options.B: 10 millilitres per hour
options.C: 100 millilitres per hour
options.D: 30 millilitres per hour

explanation: Maintaining urine output at or above 30 millilitres per hour confirms that the kidneys are receiving sufficient blood flow. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T4#BMP221_U2_T4_h4)

question: What happens during the first phase of Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation?

options.A: Blood pressure rises uncontrollably due to heart muscle failure
options.B: All blood vessels dilate permanently and prevent any clotting
options.C: The bone marrow suddenly stops producing all red blood cells
options.D: Widespread microvascular blood clots form and consume clotting factors

explanation: The first step of DIC involves many tiny clots forming throughout small blood vessels, which uses up all the available platelets and clotting proteins. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T6#BMP311_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why do healthy term newborns rely on brown adipose tissue instead of shivering when they get cold?

options.A: Shivering requires too much energy from the baby's lungs.
options.B: Their muscular and nervous systems are still too immature for effective shivering.
options.C: Shivering only occurs in adults who have fully developed sweat glands.
options.D: Brown adipose tissue is the only type of fat present in a full-term baby.

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine regarding digestive contents?

question: How many rods make up a Jadelle implant set?

question: How many enzymes in the human body rely on zinc for catalytic, structural, or regulatory functions?

question: A woman comes to the clinic at 10 weeks pregnant with heavy bleeding and lower abdominal cramps. On examination, you see the cervical os is wide open. What is the most likely diagnosis?

question: What is the main advantage of producing drugs through laboratory synthesis instead of relying only on plants?

question: Which of these skin findings is a normal variant in African newborns and not a cause for alarm?

question: Why do midwives conduct research in clinical practice?

options.D: To increase the cost of maternal health services in hospitals

question: Which of the following practices is NOT recommended when protecting a community well or borehole?

question: If a pregnant woman with bipolar disorder suddenly stops her medication out of fear, what is the main risk?

question: You need to display monthly malaria case trends over an entire year. Which chart type works best?

options.A: Line chart

question: How long should a midwife ideally postpone a newborn's first bath to ensure temperature stability?

question: Which mineral does magnesium sulfate block to help relax the uterus?

question: Why must pregnant women consume water-soluble vitamins on a regular, daily basis?

question: A skin scrape heals over several days as new cells form. Which process drives this healing?

options.A: Mitosis

question: A laboring woman with severe pre-eclampsia is about to deliver her baby. Which drug should the midwife avoid using for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Ergometrine
options.B: Normal saline
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Ringer's lactate

question: What is a primary obstetric complication of severe maternal dehydration caused by waterborne diarrheal illness?

options.A: Premature closure of the fetal anterior fontanelle bone plates

question: What is the specific emergency treatment used for severe heart collapse caused by local anaesthetic toxicity?

options.A: Calcium gluconate injection

question: Which action by a nurse represents a clear violation of professional boundaries?

question: How should pot and pan handles be positioned on a stove to prevent burns?

question: What is the very first step a midwife should take when planning a community WASH program?

options.C: Build a modern public toilet facility without consulting community members

explanation: Understanding the specific challenges and culture of a community ensures that health education addresses their real, everyday problems. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which clinical observation reported by a midwife should prompt immediate suspicion of early-onset neonatal sepsis?

options.C: Passing thick meconium stool within hours of birth
options.D: Sleeping peacefully for four hours straight at night

question: What problem can happen if very high oxygen concentrations are given for too long?

options.C: Alveolar membrane damage and oxygen toxicity
options.D: Severe iron-deficiency anemia due to red blood cell destruction

question: What attitude should a midwife maintain when discussing sensitive reproductive health topics in conservative communities?

options.A: Playful and overly casual to lighten the mood
options.B: Dismissive of local traditions and cultural beliefs
options.C: Strict and demanding of immediate behavioral change

question: Why is having a bedside commode nearby an important safety measure for these patients?

question: A child injures the growth plate in the lower end of the femur. Which anatomical region of the bone is directly affected?

question: Where does SPSS typically display results and tables after running a statistical test?

question: Which condition is a major airway-related reason for performing a tonsillectomy?

question: A midwife gives the exact same emergency care to a newborn girl as she would to a newborn boy. Which core principle is this?

question: Where should a pulse oximeter sensor be placed on a newborn to get an accurate pre-ductal oxygen reading?

question: Why are preterm infants more vulnerable to bacterial infections than full-term babies?

question: Why is dietary management an essential part of caring for older adults with chronic conditions?

options.C: It helps control symptoms and prevents disease complications

question: A woman arrives at a primary health center with severe bleeding after childbirth. Why is quick decision-making crucial here?

question: Which transmission route is primarily responsible for the rapid spread of influenza in a crowded classroom?

question: Why are corticosteroids used for short-term relief rather than long-term care in ulcerative colitis?

question: How does poor management of liquid waste directly increase malaria transmission in communities?

question: A tutor notices that mature midwifery students lose interest when lectures are too abstract. What is the best action for the tutor to take?

question: Why do community myths about eclampsia often cause severe delays in Nigeria?

question: Why must midwives be careful when recommending vitamin A supplements to pregnant women?

question: What is an effective way to support discharge counseling for mothers with low literacy levels?

question: Why is adequate fluid intake especially important for a breastfeeding mother?

question: Which part of the fetus is typically identified during the second Leopold's maneuver?

question: What is the main goal of managing a patient with no dehydration by increasing home fluids and continued feeding?

question: At what gestational age is a planned, history-based cervical stitch usually placed?

question: Which group of healthcare workers acts as frontline pillars delivering maternal and child services in Nigerian primary health centers?

question: Why should you avoid milking or stripping chest drainage tubing routinely?

question: Why is it important to check for other issues like thyroid problems when evaluating suspected andropause?

question: Which metric units are standard for recording adult height and weight in clinical midwifery practice?

question: What is the key difference between prolonged labor and obstructed labor?

question: A student midwife prepares to start an oxytocin infusion for labor induction. What is the correct dosing strategy to follow?

question: Why is drying a newborn baby thoroughly right after birth so important?

question: What dangerous event defines a strangulated hernia?

question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about drugs with a narrow therapeutic index?

question: A frightened laboring woman needs an emergency Caesarean section but refuses to sign the consent form out of panic. What should the midwife do first?

question: Why are antenatal and postnatal clinics ideal settings for identifying survivors of gender-based violence?

question: What happens immediately after mucosal blood flow drops due to prostaglandin inhibition?

question: What is the main role of Vitamin D in adolescent bone health?

question: A 16-year-old girl visits the clinic for contraception and asks if her mother will find out. What should the midwife do first?

explanation: Medications are used when anxiety is severe enough to interfere with the mother's well-being and daily functioning. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T4#BMP223_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why is discussing a patient's labor details in a hospital corridor an ethical breach?

options.A: It exposes private medical information to unauthorized people passing by

options.C: It automatically invalidates the official birth notification form

question: Why did Nigeria shift toward community-based mental health services?

options.A: To transfer all nursing responsibilities to non-medical volunteers
options.B: To eliminate the need for any medications in treating mental illness
options.C: To permanently close all hospitals and rely completely on traditional healers
options.D: To break down geographic barriers and reduce centralized institutional stigma

question: What is the most frequent side effect reported by patients receiving a course of ECT?

options.A: Inability to feel emotions

options.C: Temporary memory loss
options.D: Chronic visual blindness

question: Which communication skill helps a patient share her true feelings most effectively?

options.A: Using closed-ended questions that require only a yes or no
options.B: Giving immediate advice before letting the patient finish speaking
options.C: Asking open-ended questions and practicing active listening
options.D: Interrupting the patient frequently to speed up the clinic visit

question: What is the main effect of sympatholytic drugs on the body?

options.A: They increase adrenaline in the blood
options.B: They slow down the sympathetic nervous system
options.C: They speed up the heart rate
options.D: They cause a fight-or-flight reaction

explanation: Sympatholytic drugs block the effects of the sympathetic nervous system, whereas sympathomimetic drugs stimulate it. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T3#BMP124_U2_T3_h1)

question: Where does a community midwife mainly work?

options.C: Within rural and grassroots health clinics
options.D: Inside major tertiary teaching hospitals
